mainTopic: Holy objects and prayer near improper places; immersion for קרי during a more severe impurity; the times of the daily prayers and making up missed prayers
overview: The amud first finishes the topic of holy objects in a room used for marital relations. A chest counts as a כלי בתוך כלי, and a ספר תורה needs a ten-טפח partition, but only when there is no other room. The גמרא then limits the משנה's four אמות from צואה to צואה behind a person. If the צואה is in front, one must move until it is out of sight, and the same applies to תפלה. רב חסדא allows praying facing a בית הכסא, and the גמרא explains that he means a new one that was never used. A new משנה has רבי יהודה exempt people with a more severe impurity from טבילה for קרי, and רבי חייא confirms that this holds even when the קרי came first. After the chapter מי שמתו closes, the next chapter's משנה lists the deadlines for each תפלה. The גמרא explains that sunrise is the practice of the וָתִיקִין. Praying שחרית after noon earns credit for prayer but not for praying on time. A missed prayer can be made up at the next prayer, even across the change of day, but only if it was missed by mistake and not on purpose.

steps.title: A chest counts as a vessel within a vessel
steps.stepSummary: Ends the earlier discussion: placing a holy object on or in a chest counts as a כלי בתוך כלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Putting it on a chest is considered like a vessel inside a vessel.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the tail end of the previous discussion about how to cover holy objects in a room used for marital relations. It says that a chest counts as a double covering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the גמרא required a holy object in such a room to be inside two coverings (a כלי בתוך כלי). Here it adds that a chest, a closed storage piece of furniture, already counts as that double covering, so nothing more is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: A vessel inside a vessel, meaning a double covering
Is considered like / is similar to

steps.confusionAlert: This line starts in the middle of a thought that began on the previous עמוד. It is finishing an earlier ruling, not opening a new topic.

phrases.english: On a chest,
it is considered like a vessel within a vessel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a ruling begun on the previous amud
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A chest qualifies as a כלי בתוך כלי for covering holy objects.

steps.title: A ספר תורה in the room needs a ten-טפח partition
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי rules that a ספר תורה in a room used for marital relations needs a partition of ten טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: A ספר תורה needs a partition of ten טפחים made for it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן לוי gives a new rule: if a ספר תורה is in a room used for marital relations, a partition ten טפחים high must be put up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ספר תורה has more קדושה than other holy objects, so covering it is not enough. A ten-טפח partition halachically creates a separate space, so the scroll is treated as if it were in its own room.

keyTerms.meaning: Ten (טפחים), the standard height of a halachic partition

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule sets up the story that follows, which limits when the partition solution is allowed.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:

phrases.aramaic: סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה — צָרִיךְ לַעֲשׂוֹת לוֹ מְחִיצָּה עֲשָׂרָה.
phrases.english: A Torah scroll: one must make a partition of ten handbreadths for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from smaller holy objects to the stricter case of a ספר תורה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ספר תורה in a room used for marital relations requires a ten-טפח partition.

steps.title: מר זוטרא sees a partition in מר בר רב אשי's room
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא visits and sees that מר בר רב אשי put up a ten-טפח partition for the ספר תורה in his bedroom.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא came to the house of רב אשי. He saw that in the bedroom of מר בר רב אשי, where a ספר תורה was kept, a partition of ten טפחים had been made for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that sets up the next move. מר זוטרא sees רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule being followed in practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The scene shows the partition solution actually being used. It prepares a question about whether this solution was really needed in this particular house.

keyTerms.meaning: His place, here meaning his bedroom

phrases.aramaic: מָר זוּטְרָא אִיקְּלַע לְבֵי רַב אָשֵׁי,
phrases.english: Mar Zutra happened to come to the house of Rav Ashi,

phrases.aramaic: חַזְיֵיהּ לְדוּכְתֵּיהּ דְּמָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי
phrases.english: he saw the place (bedroom) of Mar bar Rav Ashi
in which a Torah scroll was placed
and a partition of ten had been made for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר זוּטְרָא אִיקְּלַע לְבֵי רַב אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the rule of step 2 being applied in practice
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Story setup: the ten-טפח partition was used in מר בר רב אשי's bedroom.

steps.title: The partition is only for someone with no other room
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא challenges him: רבי יהושע בן לוי allowed a partition only when there is no other room, and you have one.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Whose opinion are you following? רבי יהושע בן לוי's? Say that רבי יהושע בן לוי said this only for someone who has no other room. But you, Master, do have another room!
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא questions the practice. He argues that the partition is only a fallback for someone who has no other room to keep the ספר תורה in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge narrows רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule. The partition is a last-resort solution, not the preferred option. If another room is available, the ספר תורה should simply be moved there.

keyTerms.meaning: Say (that perhaps)…, used to limit a statement

phrases.english: He said to him: According to whom?
According to Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi?

phrases.aramaic: אֵימַר דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
phrases.english: Say that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said it
for one who has no other room;

phrases.aramaic: מָר הָא אִית לֵיהּ בֵּיתָא אַחֲרִינָא?
phrases.english: but the Master does have another room!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ כְּמַאן כְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the practice described in step 3
steps.kashyaTarget: מר בר רב אשי's use of the partition when another room was available
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule applies only when no other room exists, so using it here is not justified.

steps.title: I did not think of that
steps.stepSummary: מר בר רב אשי admits he had not considered this.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It did not occur to me.
steps.whatsHappening: מר בר רב אשי accepts the challenge and admits he simply had not thought of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His admission confirms מר זוטרא's reading. The partition is permitted only when there is no other room. When there is another room, the ספר תורה should be moved.

keyTerms.meaning: It was not on my mind / I did not think of it

steps.whatToRemember: A ten-טפח partition for a ספר תורה in a bedroom is only a fallback. If there is another room, the ספר תורה must be kept there.

phrases.english: He said to him: It did not occur to me.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concedes the challenge of step 4
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He concedes that he had not considered it, which confirms that the partition is only for when no other room exists.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: distance four אמות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: one must distance four אמות from urine and צואה.
steps.simpleTranslation: How far must one distance himself from them (urine) and from feces? Four cubits.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה and quotes it. This sets up the next move, where an אמורא will qualify the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives one fixed distance, four אמות, for saying קריאת שמע near urine or צואה. The quote brings this rule back into focus so it can be refined.

phrases.english: How far must he distance himself from them and from feces?
Four cubits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic by returning to the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One must distance four אמות from urine and צואה.

steps.title: Four cubits only when it is behind you
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא limits the four-אמות rule to צואה behind a person; if it is in front, one must distance until it is out of sight, and the same applies to תפלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said in the name of רב סחורה in the name of רב הונא: They taught this only when it is behind him. But if it is in front of him, he must distance himself as far as his eyes can see. The same is true for prayer.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא qualifies the משנה. Four אמות is enough only for צואה behind you. If it is in front of you, you must move until you can no longer see it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's four אמות is now limited to one case, צואה behind the person. Something in front of you that you can see is more disrespectful, so the distance becomes 'as far as the eye can see'. רב הונא applies the same standard to תפלה.

keyTerms.meaning: They taught this only… (introduces a limitation)
As far as his eyes can see

steps.confusionAlert: 'מלא עיניו' does not mean a set number of אמות. It means moving away until the צואה is no longer in view.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא אָמַר רַב סְחוֹרָה אָמַר רַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Rava said that Rav Seḥora said that Rav Huna said:
They taught this only when it is behind him,
but if it is in front of him, he distances himself as far as his eyes can see,
and so too for prayer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the scope of the משנה quoted in step 6
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Four אמות applies only to צואה behind a person; in front, one must distance until it is out of sight, for both קריאת שמע and תפלה.

steps.title: Challenge: one may pray facing a bathroom
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב הונא with רב חסדא's ruling that a person may stand facing a בית הכסא and pray.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But רפרם בר פפא said in the name of רב חסדא: A person may stand facing a bathroom and pray!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב הונא's rule. רב חסדא allows praying right in front of a בית הכסא, which seems to contradict the requirement to distance until it is out of sight.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If צואה in front of you requires distancing until it is out of view, how can someone pray facing a bathroom, which is visible and nearby? The two rulings appear to clash directly.

phrases.aramaic: אִינִי?! וְהָא אָמַר רַפְרָם בַּר פָּפָּא
phrases.english: Is that so?! But didn't Rafram bar Pappa say
that Rav Ḥisda said:

phrases.aramaic: עוֹמֵד אָדָם כְּנֶגֶד בֵּית הַכִּסֵּא וּמִתְפַּלֵּל!
phrases.english: A person may stand facing a bathroom and pray!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי וְהָא אָמַר רַפְרָם בַּר פָּפָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב הונא's ruling
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's rule that one must distance from צואה in front as far as the eye can see
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב חסדא permits praying directly facing a bathroom, which contradicts any need to distance.

steps.title: Answer: a bathroom with no feces in it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב חסדא is speaking about a בית הכסא that has no צואה in it.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? A bathroom that has no feces in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by limiting רב חסדא's case to an empty bathroom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא's rule is about actual צואה. If the bathroom is empty, there is nothing to distance from, so praying facing it is fine. The two rulings would then address different cases.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? (introduces a narrowing answer)

phrases.english: With what are we dealing here?
With a bathroom that has no feces in it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 8
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב חסדא appeared to allow prayer facing any bathroom.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב חסדא refers only to a bathroom with no צואה, so there is no contradiction.

steps.title: Challenge: an empty bathroom still counts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the answer with רב יוסף בר חנינא's teaching that a בית הכסא keeps its status even when empty.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But רב יוסף בר חנינא said: The bathroom the Sages spoke of applies even if there is no feces in it, and the bathhouse they spoke of applies even if there is no person in it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the previous answer. רב יוסף בר חנינא teaches that a bathroom is treated as a bathroom even when it is empty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A place set aside and used as a בית הכסא keeps its improper status because of what it is, not because of what is in it right now. The same is true of a בית המרחץ even when no one is in it. So 'an empty bathroom' cannot explain רב חסדא's leniency.

phrases.aramaic: אִינִי?! וְהָאָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף בַּר חֲנִינָא:
phrases.english: Is that so?! But didn't Rav Yosef bar Ḥanina say:
The bathroom that they spoke of

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ צוֹאָה
phrases.english: applies even though there is no feces in it,
and the bathhouse that they spoke of

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ אָדָם!
phrases.english: applies even though there is no person in it!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי וְהָאָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף בַּר חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 9
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that רב חסדא refers to an empty bathroom
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An empty bathroom keeps its status as a bathroom, so emptiness cannot explain the leniency.

steps.title: Final answer: a brand-new bathroom
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that רב חסדא means a newly built בית הכסא that has never been used.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what case are we dealing with here? A new one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer. רב חסדא is talking about a newly built bathroom that has not yet been used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף בר חנינא's rule covers a bathroom that has been used, even if it is empty right now. A new structure that has never been used is not covered by that rule, so רב חסדא can allow praying facing it. Whether designating it as a bathroom alone gives it that status is raised in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: New ones, meaning a newly built, unused bathroom

steps.whatToRemember: Four אמות is enough only for צואה behind you; in front, you must distance until it is out of sight, for both קריאת שמע and תפלה. A used בית הכסא keeps its status even when empty, but a brand-new unused one does not, so one may pray facing it.
steps.confusionAlert: 'חדתי' does not mean a bathroom that was just cleaned. It means a new structure that has never been used as a bathroom.

phrases.english: Rather, with what are we dealing here?
With new ones.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer of step 9 after the challenge of step 10
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב חסדא's case was an empty bathroom, but that was rejected.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב חסדא refers to a newly built bathroom that has not yet been used, so one may stand facing it and pray.

steps.title: Designation seems to leave the ruling uncertain
steps.stepSummary: רבינא had asked whether designating a place as a בית הכסא gives it that status. That uncertainty challenges the previous answer about a newly built, unused בית הכסא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn’t רבינא ask: If someone designated a place as a בית הכסא, what is its status? Does designation take effect or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer that prayer is permitted facing a newly built, unused בית הכסא. רבינא’s question suggests its status may still be uncertain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous answer relied on the fact that the בית הכסא had never been used. But if designation alone counts, its lack of use might not settle the issue.

phrases.english: But didn’t Ravina have this question:
If he designated it as a bathroom, what is the law?
Does designation take effect, or does designation not take effect?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer that the בית הכסא is newly built and has never been used.
steps.kashyaTarget: The use of an unused בית הכסא to explain why prayer facing it is permitted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If designation alone gives the place בית הכסא status, being unused may not be enough to permit prayer facing it.

steps.title: The uncertainty concerns prayer at the place, not facing it
steps.stepSummary: רבינא’s question concerned standing and praying inside the designated place. Prayer facing it was not in doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבינא asked his question, he meant standing there to pray inside it. But as for praying facing it—no, that was not his question.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by narrowing רבינא’s question. It was about prayer at the designated place itself, not prayer facing it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A designated but unused בית הכסא may raise a question about using that very place for prayer. That does not challenge the earlier ruling about standing opposite it.

phrases.english: When Ravina had his question,
it concerned standing there to pray inside it;
but facing it—no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the scope of רבינא’s question, removing the challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes prayer at the designated place from prayer facing it.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבינא was uncertain even about praying opposite a designated, unused בית הכסא.
steps.terutzMaskana: His uncertainty concerns standing there to pray inside it; facing it is not included.

steps.title: Persian-style בתי כסא are treated as sealed
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a special ruling for Persian-style בתי כסא: even when they contain צואה, they are treated as sealed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: These Persian-style בתי כסא, even though they have צואה in them, are considered sealed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds a related ruling about a particular kind of בית הכסא. Its צואה does not receive the same treatment as exposed צואה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling turns on how these בתי כסא are treated: as sealed, despite containing צואה. It is a special outcome for this type of בית הכסא, not a denial that it is a בית הכסא.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא: הָנֵי בָּתֵּי כִּסָּאֵי דְּפָרְסָאֵי
phrases.english: Rava said: These Persian bathrooms,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּאִית בְּהוּ צוֹאָה —
phrases.english: even though they contain feces,
are considered sealed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: הָנֵי בָּתֵּי כִּסָּאֵי דְּפָרְסָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a distinct, related ruling after the discussion of an unused בית הכסא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Persian-style בתי כסא are considered sealed despite containing צואה.

steps.title: טבילה when another impurity is already present
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists people who acquire an additional impurity and says they require טבילה. רבי יהודה exempts them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says that a זב who experienced קרי, a נידה who discharged semen, and a woman who had relations and then saw menstrual blood require טבילה. רבי יהודה exempts them.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins a different discussion. It gives three cases in which the impurity of קרי (semen) is combined with a more severe impurity (זיבה or נדה); in the third case the קרי comes first and the נדה follows. The first opinion requires טבילה in all three.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ruling still requires טבילה in these cases. רבי יהודה disagrees and exempts them; the next גמרא will examine the reach of his exemption.

keyTerms.meaning: a man with a discharge that causes ritual impurity

phrases.english: Mishna: A zav who experienced a seminal emission,
and a menstruating woman who discharged semen,
and a woman who had relations and then saw menstrual blood—
require immersion. But Rabbi Yehuda exempts them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה on טבילה rather than continuing the discussion of בתי כסא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first opinion requires טבילה in all three listed cases; רבי יהודה exempts them.

steps.title: Does the order of impurities change רבי יהודה’s ruling?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about someone who had קרי first and then developed זיבה. Does רבי יהודה still exempt him from טבילה?
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא asks: According to רבי יהודה, what if a בעל קרי later has זיבה? Perhaps רבי יהודה exempted only a זב who later had קרי, because he was already unable to become pure through that טבילה. A בעל קרי was initially able to immerse—does he therefore remain obligated, or is there no difference?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new question about רבי יהודה’s exemption. It reverses the order in the משנה’s first case and explains why that order might matter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה’s case, the person was already a זב before experiencing קרי, so טבילה for קרי would not remove his existing impurity. In the new case, he first became a בעל קרי, when טבילה could have helped him; the question is whether that earlier obligation remains.

keyTerms.meaning: a person who experienced a seminal emission
a discharge that causes זב impurity
someone for whom immersion could be effective

phrases.english: Gemara: A question was raised before them:
A person who had a seminal emission and then saw a discharge,
what is the law according to Rabbi Yehuda?
When Rabbi Yehuda exempted someone there,
in the case of a zav who experienced a seminal emission,
that was because from the outset he was not fit for immersion;
But someone who first had a seminal emission and then saw a discharge,
who, from the outset, could have benefited from immersion,
is he obligated, or perhaps there is no difference?

steps.triggerLanguage: גְּמָ׳ אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: בַּעַל קֶרִי, שֶׁרָאָה זִיבָה לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה מַהוּ?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests whether רבי יהודה’s exemption in the משנה also applies when קרי comes before זיבה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי יהודה requires טבילה when a בעל קרי later develops זיבה, or exempts him as he does a זב who later experiences קרי.

steps.title: A similar case points to רבי יהודה’s answer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא compares a woman who became נידה after relations to a בעל קרי who later saw זיבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: A woman who had relations and then saw menstrual blood requires immersion, but רבי יהודה exempts her. Isn’t her case like that of a בעל קרי who later saw זיבה? רבי יהודה exempts her, so we can infer his answer for the other case.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a case from the משנה to answer the question raised in the previous step. It argues that רבי יהודה’s ruling there should apply to the similar case of a בעל קרי who later saw זיבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both cases, a later, more severe impurity follows an earlier reason for טבילה. Since רבי יהודה exempts the woman from this טבילה, the גמרא infers that he also exempts the בעל קרי in the case being asked about.

keyTerms.meaning: a person who had a seminal emission
a discharge that causes a more severe impurity
the sage whose exemption is being examined

phrases.english: Come and hear: A woman who had relations and then saw menstrual blood
requires immersion, but Rabbi Yehuda exempts her.
But isn’t a woman who had relations and then saw menstrual blood
like someone who had a seminal emission and then saw a discharge?
And Rabbi Yehuda exempts her.
Infer the answer from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an analogous case to answer the question in step 16.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהודה exempts a בעל קרי who later saw זיבה from the טבילה under discussion.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה’s case of a woman who became נידה after relations.

steps.title: רבי חייא states the answer directly
steps.stepSummary: A teaching of רבי חייא explicitly gives רבי יהודה’s ruling for the exact case in question.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא taught explicitly: A בעל קרי who then saw זיבה requires טבילה, but רבי יהודה exempts him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives a direct teaching about the בעל קרי who later saw זיבה. It confirms the answer that the previous comparison suggested.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier proof depended on comparing two cases. This teaching names the questioned case itself, so no comparison is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: the sage who taught this statement

steps.whatToRemember: For the case asked about, רבי יהודה exempts the בעל קרי who later saw זיבה from the טבילה under discussion.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥiyya taught explicitly:
Someone who had a seminal emission and then saw a discharge
requires immersion, but Rabbi Yehuda exempts him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms the inferred answer with an explicit teaching.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהודה exempts a בעל קרי who later saw זיבה from this טבילה.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing מי שמתו
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula marks the end of the chapter מי שמתו.
steps.simpleTranslation: We shall return to you, ‘One whose dead.’
steps.whatsHappening: The chapter מי שמתו ends here. This is a closing line, not another argument about טבילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous question has been answered. The next line will begin a new chapter and a new subject.

keyTerms.meaning: the name of the chapter being closed

phrases.english: We shall return to you, ‘One whose dead.’

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after its final question is answered.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The chapter מי שמתו is complete.

steps.title: The new משנה gives the morning prayer deadline
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה begins with two opinions on the latest time for תפילת השחר.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: תפילת השחר may be said until noon. רבי יהודה says: Until four hours into the day.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens the next chapter by giving the time limit for תפילת השחר. It first states one deadline, then רבי יהודה’s earlier deadline.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion allows תפילת השחר until midday. רבי יהודה limits it to the first four hours of the day.

phrases.english: Mishnah: The morning prayer is until midday.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: עַד אַרְבַּע שָׁעוֹת.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: Until four hours into the day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new chapter and a new topic after the closing formula.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תפילת השחר is permitted until midday according to the first opinion, or until four hours into the day according to רבי יהודה.

steps.title: The משנה gives the afternoon prayer deadline
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives two time limits for תפילת המנחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: תפילת המנחה may be said until evening. רבי יהודה says: Until פלג המנחה, the midpoint of the afternoon period.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to תפילת המנחה. It gives an evening deadline and then רבי יהודה’s earlier deadline.
steps.deeperAnalysis: As with the morning prayer, the two opinions disagree about how late this prayer may be said. The משנה names רבי יהודה’s limit פלג המנחה without explaining its calculation here.

keyTerms.meaning: the midpoint of the afternoon prayer period

phrases.english: The afternoon prayer is until evening,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: עַד פְּלַג הַמִּנְחָה.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: Until the midpoint of the afternoon period.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה’s list of prayer times, moving from morning to afternoon.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תפילת המנחה may be said until evening according to the first opinion, or until פלג המנחה according to רבי יהודה.

steps.title: The evening prayer has no fixed deadline
steps.stepSummary: The משנה describes תפילת הערב differently from the preceding prayers.
steps.simpleTranslation: The evening prayer has no fixed time.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now turns to תפילת הערב. Instead of giving an hour as its deadline, it says the prayer has no fixed time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line does not give a cutoff like חצות or פלג המנחה. It means תפילת הערב may be said throughout the night; the גמרא later discusses what else 'no fixed time' implies.

phrases.english: The evening prayer has no fixed time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list with the evening prayer, using different wording from the earlier time limits.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תפילת הערב has no fixed time.

steps.title: The משנה gives the additional prayer deadline
steps.stepSummary: The משנה ends its list with two time limits for the מוסף prayer.
steps.simpleTranslation: The מוסף prayer may be said all day. רבי יהודה says: Until seven hours into the day.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its list with the מוסף prayer. It allows the prayer all day under the first opinion, while רבי יהודה gives an earlier limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is another disagreement about the latest time for a prayer. The first opinion says all day; רבי יהודה says until seven hours into the day.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה lists four prayers: morning, afternoon, evening, and מוסף. It gives competing deadlines for three of them and says תפילת הערב has no fixed time.

phrases.english: And the additional prayer is all day,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: עַד שֶׁבַע שָׁעוֹת.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: Until seven hours into the day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the משנה’s list of prayer times.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מוסף prayer may be said all day according to the first opinion, or until seven hours into the day according to רבי יהודה.

steps.title: Why does another teaching point to sunrise?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sets a teaching about sunrise against the משנה’s later time limit for תפילת השחר.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא raises a contradiction: The proper time for its מצוה is at sunrise, so that one joins גאולה to תפילה and ends up praying during the day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה’s time limit for תפילת השחר. Another teaching seems to place the prayer right at sunrise.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The teaching describes finishing קריאת שמע around sunrise and then moving straight from גאולה into תפילה. The question is whether that sunrise practice leaves room for the later times allowed by the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Redemption, mentioned in the blessing after קריאת שמע
He should place immediately next to

phrases.english: Gemara: And they raised a contradiction:
Its proper time is at sunrise,
so that he joins redemption directly to prayer,
and thus finds himself praying during the day!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the משנה’s list of prayer times ends, the גמרא returns to the time for תפילת השחר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה’s allowance to pray תפילת השחר later in the morning.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A teaching that places the ideal sequence at sunrise appears to conflict with a later permitted time.

steps.title: Sunrise describes the practice of the especially careful
steps.stepSummary: The sunrise teaching describes וָתִיקִין, rather than setting the only permitted time for everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: That teaching refers to the especially careful. רבי יוחנן said that they would finish it at sunrise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the sunrise challenge by identifying whom that teaching describes. It is speaking about וָתִיקִין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The וָתִיקִין finished קריאת שמע at sunrise so they could pray immediately afterward. Their careful timing does not remove the later time allowed by the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: People especially careful in observing מצוות
The sage quoted to explain the sunrise practice

phrases.english: When that teaching was taught, it referred to the especially careful.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: וָתִיקִין הָיוּ גּוֹמְרִים אוֹתָהּ
phrases.english: For Rabbi Yoḥanan said: The especially careful would finish it
at sunrise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It limits the sunrise teaching to a particular group, answering step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The teaching describes a special practice rather than an exclusive time limit.
steps.terutzMaskana: Sunrise is the practice of וָתִיקִין; the משנה’s later times still apply.

steps.title: Can a missed morning prayer be made up after noon?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the noon limit with רבי יוחנן’s ruling that a missed שחרית is prayed at מנחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is noon really the latest possible time? רבי יוחנן said that someone who missed the evening prayer prays twice in the morning, and someone who missed the morning prayer prays twice in the afternoon.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new challenge to the noon limit. A ruling about missed prayers allows two prayers at מנחה when שחרית was missed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מנחה comes after noon. If the missed שחרית can still be prayed then, the noon limit needs explaining.

phrases.aramaic: וְכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא עַד חֲצוֹת וְתוּ לָא,
phrases.english: And does everyone agree: only until noon and no later?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַב מָרִי בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא
phrases.english: But didn’t Rav Mari, son of Rav Huna,
son of Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: טָעָה וְלֹא הִתְפַּלֵּל עַרְבִית
phrases.english: say that Rabbi Yoḥanan said: If one erred and did not pray the evening prayer,
he prays twice at the morning prayer;
if he missed the morning prayer, he prays twice at the afternoon prayer.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא עַד חֲצוֹת וְתוּ לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: With the sunrise question answered, the גמרא now tests the other end of the permitted time.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the noon limit prevents any later prayer for a missed שחרית.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן allows a missed שחרית to be prayed at מנחה, which is after noon.

steps.title: A later prayer does not earn credit for praying on time
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא distinguishes between receiving credit for a prayer and receiving credit for praying it at its appointed time.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may continue praying through the day. Until noon, one receives credit for prayer at its proper time; afterward, one receives credit for prayer, but not for prayer at its proper time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a prayer can still receive credit after noon. What ends at noon is the credit for praying שחרית on time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This explains how a missed שחרית can be prayed at מנחה without changing the earlier time limit. The prayer still counts as prayer, but it is not an on-time שחרית.

keyTerms.meaning: Credit for a prayer at its appointed time

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read “the whole day” as extending the on-time window for שחרית. The answer expressly denies on-time credit after noon.
steps.whatToRemember: After noon, a missed שחרית can still receive credit as prayer, but not as prayer at its proper time.

phrases.english: He may continue praying throughout the day;
until noon, they give him
credit for a prayer at its appointed time;
from then onward,
they give him credit for a prayer,

phrases.aramaic: שְׂכַר תְּפִלָּה בִּזְמַנָּהּ — לָא יָהֲבִי לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: but they do not give him credit for a prayer at its appointed time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It resolves the apparent conflict between the noon limit and the later prayer for a missed שחרית.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes prayer credit from credit for praying at the appointed time.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If a missed שחרית is prayed after noon, noon cannot be a meaningful limit.
steps.terutzMaskana: Noon limits on-time credit; a later prayer can still receive prayer credit.

steps.title: Can a missed afternoon prayer be made up at night?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether someone who missed מִנְחָה by mistake may pray twice at עַרְבִית.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: If someone erred and did not pray the afternoon prayer, may he pray the evening prayer twice?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about a missed מִנְחָה. It is setting up two possible ways to answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person missed the prayer through error, not by choice. The question is whether the next prayer, עַרְבִית, can also make up the missed one.

phrases.aramaic: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: טָעָה וְלֹא הִתְפַּלֵּל מִנְחָה,
phrases.english: They asked: If someone erred and did not pray the afternoon prayer,
may he pray the evening prayer twice?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 27 distinguished making up a prayer from praying it at its appointed time; this step asks whether making it up works across the change of day.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: May someone who missed מִנְחָה by mistake make it up by praying twice at עַרְבִית?

steps.title: Why the change of day might prevent a makeup prayer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא considers whether making up עַרְבִית at שַׁחֲרִית works only because both fall within one day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even if someone who missed the evening prayer prays twice in the morning because evening and morning form one day, perhaps the afternoon prayer is different: prayer takes the place of a sacrifice, and once a sacrifice’s day has passed, it is lost.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the answer to the new question might be no. It is comparing a missed מִנְחָה with a missed עַרְבִית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עַרְבִית followed by שַׁחֲרִית can be viewed as part of one day. מִנְחָה followed by עַרְבִית crosses into a new day, so the time limit of a קׇרְבָּן might prevent making it up.

keyTerms.meaning: its sacrifice can no longer be brought

phrases.aramaic: אִם תִּמְצָא לוֹמַר, טָעָה וְלֹא הִתְפַּלֵּל עַרְבִית
phrases.english: Even if you say that someone erred and did not pray the evening prayer

phrases.aramaic: מִתְפַּלֵּל שַׁחֲרִית שְׁתַּיִם, מִשּׁוּם דְּחַד יוֹמָא הוּא,
phrases.english: prays twice at the morning prayer because it is one day,

phrases.aramaic: דִּכְתִיב: ״וַיְהִי עֶרֶב וַיְהִי בֹקֶר יוֹם אֶחָד״,
phrases.english: as it is written: ‘And there was evening and there was morning, one day,’

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָכָא תְּפִלָּה בִּמְקוֹם קׇרְבָּן הִיא,
phrases.english: but here, prayer takes the place of a sacrifice,
and once its day has passed, its sacrifice is lost.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Develops the reason that the makeup prayer asked about in step 28 might not be allowed.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does crossing into a new day prevent making up מִנְחָה, even if a missed עַרְבִית can be made up at שַׁחֲרִית?

steps.title: Why prayer might still be possible later
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers the other side: perhaps prayer, as a request for mercy, can still be said later.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps, since prayer is a request for mercy, a person may continue praying whenever he wishes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the other possible answer to its question. This prepares for a ruling that will choose between the two sides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The comparison to a קׇרְבָּן suggested a strict end time. Viewing תְּפִלָּה as a request for mercy suggests that crossing into the next day need not prevent making it up.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִילְמָא כֵּיוָן דִּצְלוֹתָא רַחֲמֵי הִיא,
phrases.english: Or perhaps, since prayer is a request for mercy,
whenever he wishes, he may continue praying.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the possibility opposite to the time-limit argument in step 29.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the nature of תְּפִלָּה as a request for mercy allow the missed prayer to be made up after the day changes?

steps.title: A ruling permits two evening prayers
steps.stepSummary: A teaching from רבי יוחנן answers that someone who missed מִנְחָה by mistake prays twice at עַרְבִית.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רב הונא בר יהודה said that רבי יצחק said that רבי יוחנן said: One who erred and did not pray מנחה prays twice at ערבית. The rule that a קרבן is lost when its day passes does not apply here.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ruling that answers the question directly. Missing מִנְחָה by mistake can be made up at עַרְבִית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling addresses the exact case under discussion, rather than only a similar case. It explicitly rejects using the expired-day rule of a קׇרְבָּן to block this makeup prayer.

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע דְּאָמַר רַב הוּנָא בַּר יְהוּדָה
phrases.english: Come and hear what Rav Huna bar Yehuda said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: that Rabbi Yitzḥak said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:

phrases.aramaic: טָעָה וְלֹא הִתְפַּלֵּל מִנְחָה — מִתְפַּלֵּל עַרְבִית שְׁתַּיִם,
phrases.english: One who erred and did not pray the afternoon prayer prays twice at the evening prayer,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין בָּזֶה מִשּׁוּם דְּעָבַר יוֹמוֹ בָּטַל קׇרְבָּנוֹ.
phrases.english: and the rule that a sacrifice is lost when its day passes does not apply here.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע דְּאָמַר רַב הוּנָא בַּר יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the two possibilities by stating that the missed prayer may be made up.
steps.raayaObject: A missed מִנְחָה may be made up at עַרְבִית despite the change of day.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ruling transmitted by רב הונא בר יהודה in the name of רבי יצחק and רבי יוחנן.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives the practical answer to the question posed in step 28.

steps.title: A teaching says missed prayers cannot be repaired
steps.stepSummary: A teaching describes missed קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע and prayers as something that cannot be corrected, apparently challenging the makeup ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: They object: ‘What is crooked cannot be made straight, and what is missing cannot be counted.’ ‘What is crooked cannot be made straight’ refers to one who omitted the evening or morning קריאת שמע, or the evening or morning תפילה. ‘What is missing cannot be counted’ refers to someone whose friends joined together for a מצוה, but he did not join them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ruling with a teaching that calls an omitted prayer impossible to repair. The challenge sets up a need to distinguish which kind of omission the teaching means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If every missed prayer were beyond repair, praying twice later would not help. The passage about friends missing a shared מִצְוָה is part of the quoted teaching; the challenge to the ruling comes from its statement about missed prayer.

phrases.english: They object: ‘What is crooked cannot be made straight,
and what is missing cannot be counted.’
‘What is crooked cannot be made straight’—

phrases.aramaic: זֶה שֶׁבִּטֵּל קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע שֶׁל עַרְבִית
phrases.english: this refers to one who omitted the evening recitation of Shema
or the morning recitation of Shema,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ תְּפִלָּה שֶׁל עַרְבִית אוֹ תְּפִלָּה שֶׁל שַׁחֲרִית.
phrases.english: or the evening prayer or the morning prayer.
‘And what is missing cannot be counted’—
this refers to one whose friends joined together for a מצוה,
but he did not join them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the permission to make up a missed prayer in step 31.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן’s ruling that a missed prayer can be made up at the next prayer.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The quoted teaching says that omitting a prayer is a loss that cannot be corrected; if that includes an accidental omission, it conflicts with the ruling.

steps.title: The teaching concerns an intentional omission
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that the teaching’s unrepairable omission is one done deliberately.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said that רבי יוחנן said: What case are we discussing here? One in which the person deliberately omitted the prayer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by limiting the teaching to deliberate omission. The earlier ruling remains about someone who missed prayer by mistake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two sources address different cases. A person who missed prayer accidentally can pray twice at the next prayer; the teaching’s ‘cannot be repaired’ applies when the person deliberately skipped it.

keyTerms.meaning: what case are we discussing here?

steps.whatToRemember: For תַּשְׁלוּמִין, the distinction here is between a missed prayer through error and one omitted deliberately.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzḥak said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
What case are we discussing here? One in which he deliberately omitted it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the teaching cited in the challenge so that it does not contradict the earlier ruling.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes an intentional omission from an accidental one.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The challenging teaching seemed to say that any missed prayer, even one missed by mistake, cannot be made up.
steps.terutzMaskana: The teaching concerns deliberate omission; the ruling allowing a makeup prayer concerns error.

steps.title: The wording supports the distinction
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי points to the teaching’s choice of בִּטֵּל rather than טָעָה as support for רבי יוחנן’s answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: The wording is precise too. It says בִּטֵּל (“omitted”), not טָעָה (“made a mistake”). Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי checks the exact word used in the teaching that challenged the makeup ruling. He finds support for the answer that the teaching concerns a deliberate omission.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The teaching says בִּטֵּל, not טָעָה. That choice supports reading its unrepairable case as deliberate, while a prayer missed by mistake can still be made up.
steps.whatToRemember: The challenge does not overturn makeup prayer for someone who made a mistake; the teaching’s wording supports limiting its warning to deliberate omission.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: The wording is precise too,
because it teaches “omitted,”
and does not teach “made a mistake,”
learn from this.
